title: On the sharp Hölder exponent in the De Giorgi--Nash--Moser theory
summary: We consider solutions of uniformly elliptic equations with measurable coefficients. We assume that the lowest eigenvalue of the coefficient matrix is at least $K^{-1}$ and the largest eigenvalue is at most $K$. In three and higher dimensions we construct $α$-Hölder continuous solutions with $α= \exp(- c_n K)$. This disproves a long-standing conjecture by showing that, except for the two-dimensional case, the Hölder exponent obtained from the Bombieri--Giusti Harnack inequality has the optimal dependence on the ellipticity constant $K$.
